CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual visit

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female here for her annual visit. She reports struggling with depression off and on over the past year, which she attributes to being trapped inside and working remotely. She is currently taking Prozac 20 milligrams daily, which has helped her in the past, and she believes increasing the dose may help her through this difficult period. She has chronic back pain that bothers her when sitting for long periods at her desk at work. Symptoms improve when she stands up or changes position. She reports a small amount of numbing but denies tingling or pain down her legs. She describes the numbing as feeling like her legs are falling asleep. She denies leg weakness. She is able to perform activities of daily living, exercise, and go to the store, though symptoms are bothersome with both prolonged sitting and prolonged standing. She has a significant history of congenital coronary artery for which she underwent coronary artery bypass grafting at a young age. She reports her heart has been doing well and her arteries have been looking good.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for depression and chronic back pain as noted in history of present illness. Denies tingling or pain down legs. Denies leg weakness.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Chronic back pain
Congenital coronary artery, status post coronary artery bypass grafting

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 milligrams daily
Aspirin 81 milligrams daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works at a desk job. Has been working remotely over the past year.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Does not appear in distress
Neck: No thyroid enlargement
Heart: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable
Lungs: Clear
Abdomen: Soft
Lumbar spine: Pain to palpation, decreased flexion
Lower extremities: Good strength, no edema

RESULTS
ECG: Basically unchanged from last year
Lumbar spine x-ray: Stable from last year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Chronic back pain: Patient referred to physical therapy for management. Patient declined pain medication at this time, preferring to start with physical therapy.
Depression: Prozac increased from 20 milligrams to 40 milligrams once daily.
Cardiac: Continue aspirin 81 milligrams daily. Echocardiogram ordered.
Nurse will assist with scheduling appointments.
